items.title: neutral-stance-instructions-disagree
items.claim: Image #6 says every move requires holding a stance and then a technique, but its Lunge Punch row shows a centred stance plus forward technique, and Image #2 explicitly permits leaving the stance centred.
items.reason: A new player receives conflicting instructions about whether the stance stick must be moved to attack.
items.suggest: Replace the reference instruction with: “Choose a stance or leave that stick centred, then push the technique stick.”

items.title: mixed-score-outgrows-hud
items.claim: In Image #8, HasanAbi’s stacked half-point fraction extends below the neighbouring name plate and timer, unlike Asmongold’s zero.
items.reason: The mixed score becomes a vertically scattered element rather than an immediately readable score beside the fighter’s name.
items.suggest: Render mixed scores as a single horizontal unit with a compact ½ glyph, and verify the entire unit stays within the score container at 390×844.

items.title: controls-lose-direction-labels
items.claim: Image #15 shows directional markers on both sticks without the direction-to-action legend visible in Image #3.
items.reason: The words “STANCE” and “TECHNIQUE” alone do not tell an unfamiliar player which direction punches, kicks, jumps, or crouches.
items.suggest: Keep a compact, readable action legend available beside the sticks, with an explicit player-controlled option to hide it.

items.title: reference-bottom-is-obscured
items.claim: In Image #6, the Back Kick row at the bottom is visibly darkened by a fade while the preceding technique rows remain unobscured.
items.reason: A player consulting the move list cannot read that visible row as clearly as the other entries.
items.suggest: Remove the fade over readable list content and use a separate scroll cue outside the technique rows.

items.title: kick-extension-unverified
items.claim: Images #13, #19, and #22 label the move “FRONT KICK” while showing a bent attacking knee, but these stills do not establish whether the animation includes a fully extended kick.
items.reason: The pictured pose alone cannot settle whether players receive a clear visual indication of the kick’s reach or contact.
items.suggest: Capture the complete Front Kick sequence with simulation phase and frame identifiers; change the active pose only if that evidence shows the extension is missing.
